# BRIDGE_NOTES: RQ-PLAN-BUS-THREADS-B

## Summary

Shared local task board for cooperating agents and machines, with durable bus
threads and task ownership backed by real fenced fleet queue claims.

- `src/core/fleet/shared-store.ts`: new `handoffClaim(ref, machineId)` transfers
  a live `claimed` lease under the existing queue lock. It allocates a fresh
  epoch and owner token, rewrites the owner key, and fences the previous
  capability. It refuses expired, executing, exact-match-failing, same-owner,
  invalid and oversized recipients; returns `null` on lock contention or an
  unreadable queue rather than mutating state.
- `src/core/fleet/bus-delivery.ts` (new): durable delivery record with v1
  envelope routing metadata, thread ID, sender, recipient, ISO timestamp and
  `content.trust: 'untrusted'`. `presentBusBoardText` rewraps content under a
  fresh unpredictable delimiter on every read; `busBoardHop` projects
  metadata-only hops (id, thread, sender, recipient, timestamp).
- `src/core/fleet/bus-board.ts` (new): `BusBoard` persists threads, tasks and
  deliveries under a private, owned, non-symlink root (0600 state, 0700 dir,
  local-store lock, atomic writes, fsync, 10k records / 16 MiB bounds; corrupt
  state is refused, never reset). Thread membership gates reads, posts and all
  task verbs; posts snapshot members so late joins never receive earlier
  messages. A task names one fleet item ID (unique board-wide); claim, renew,
  release and handoff validate the exact live `SharedStore` generation before
  mutating. Capability fields (ownerToken/ownerKey/queueId) never leave board
  state or CLI output. If the board write fails after a fleet mutation, the
  orphaned claimed lease stays fenced until expiry; nothing fabricates success
  or steals it back. `foundry.eventBus: false` refuses every verb before writes.
- `src/core/fleet/event-bus.ts`: new `bus:delivery` lifecycle event kind
  (frozen delivery payload), emitted best-effort after durable commit.
- `src/cli/fleet-bus.ts` (new): thin dispatcher for `phm bus thread|task` with
  strict arity, `--peer`, `--json`, `--root`, `--queue-root`, `--` literal
  handling, exit 0/1/2, and a fixed safe-error allowlist so private paths and
  filesystem errors never reach output. Honors `fleet.sharedQueue` filesystem
  mode (`path` + `trustedCoherentStorage: true`), then board at `<path>/bus`.
- Wiring: `src/cli/fleet-subcommand-registry.ts` (`bus` lazy entry),
  `src/cli/index.ts` (top-level `bus` delegates to fleet), `src/cli/completions.ts`
  (`bus` top-level + fleet verb + subcommands), `src/cli/help.ts` (help entry).
- Docs: `docs/BUS-THREADS.md` (usage, ownership, untrusted-content and storage

against the merged receipt-batch recovery path. Backlog reconciliation only — no
new feature, no production edit was warranted (see matrix).

| 14 | Status naming — `status: 'success' \| <reason string>` (L67, L124, L129) | `outcome: 'bound' \| 'failed' \| 'not-started'` + `reason: string \| null` (await-batch.ts:52–58) | RENAMED — live consumers use new names: CLI exit `failed+notStarted===0` (cli:151), NDJSON entry/summary events (cli:39–41,144), MCP report (mcp:62–78), replan outcome routing (replan:34,84–105) |
| 15 | Doc schema — `{version:1, requests:[{id,repo,run,attempt,artifactName}]}` (L85) | `{version:1, targets:[{repo,run,attempt,artifactName}]}` exact-2-keys (await-batch.ts:121–128) | RENAMED — old schema refused by new parser (Test 1) |
| 16 | Single-shot discovery, no wait, no deadline/signal | Await-then-discover: poll attempt-meta + artifact list until present/terminal, then the SAME `discoverCiReceiptPrior` binder (await.ts:162–186); shared deadline ≤1 h + `AbortSignal` + explicit `not-started` tail (await-batch.ts:167–211) | SUPERSET — the old already-present case binds on first poll (T1); the pending case (T3) is capability the old module lacked; deadline is the intended bound |
| 17 | Two-step API — `validateBatchCiReceipt(parsed)` → `ValidatedRequest[] \| null`, then `processBatchCiReceipts({requests, gh})` (L78, L115) | `parseCiReceiptAwaitBatchInput(text)` → `{ok,targets}` \| `{ok:false,reason}`, then `awaitCiReceiptBatch(targets, opts, deps)` with internal re-validation (await-batch.ts:117, 167–176) | PRESERVED shape; reason codes replace bare `null`; bounded `timeoutMs`/`pollMs` now required |

Canonical home: `ci-resume-inputs.ts:38`. `CiResumeReceiptsFetch` import is also unused in the old file | n/a | Old file cannot compile on master as written — the merged path is the living contract. `discoverCiReceiptPrior` signature is unchanged (discovery.ts:99–101) and is exactly what `awaitCiReceipt` calls (await.ts:173–174) |

## Old `id` vs exact identity, and status naming — consumer dependency

- Old contract: caller-chosen `id` label echoed in results, dedup by `id`,
  `status: 'success' | <reason>`.
- Current contract: no `id` anywhere; each entry carries the exact
  `repo/run/attempt/artifactName` identity; `outcome` enum + `reason`.
- **No consumer depends on the old contract.** Evidence:
  - `git grep` on the worktree for `validateBatchCiReceipt`,
    `processBatchCiReceipts`, `BatchCiReceiptRequest`, `BatchCiReceiptResult`,
    `ci-receipt-batch.js` (excluding await-batch/batch-replan): zero hits.
  - The PR's entire unique diff is the one module file — it was never wired to
    a CLI command, MCP tool, or test.
  - All live consumers (`cmdFleetCiReceiptAwaitBatch`,
    `fleet_ci_receipt_await_batch`, `parseCiReceiptBatchReplanInput`) consume
    the merged contract and could not consume `{id, status}` results.
- The dropped `id` was a caller label, not evidence: correlation is strictly
  better served by the exact identity tuple the entries now echo, and dedup on
  exact identity refuses redundant double-fetches the old per-`id` check allowed.

## Remaining gaps

**None.** Every old requirement maps to an equal-or-stronger current behavior.
Documented semantic deltas (all stricter or additive, none losses):

- await adds a per-poll attempt-metadata GET that must prove exact
  repo/run/attempt identity before binding — stronger evidence gate, one extra
  read per poll vs old single-shot discovery.
- Dedup key: caller `id` → exact identity tuple (case-insensitive repo).
- Diagnostics: per-result array → pooled, target-tagged, 200-line-capped list.
- Required bounded `timeoutMs`/`pollMs` (≤1 h shared deadline) replaces the old
  unbounded per-request loop — the intended batch bound.
- Reason sanitization gains `scrubSecrets` + control/VT stripping (old was a
  raw 160-char slice).
- Old top-level unknown keys were ignored; new doc requires exactly
  `{version, targets}`.

## Supersession recommendation

PR #3648 is **fully superseded** by the merged
RQ-PHX-CIRECEIPTAWAITBATCH05SRZ1 path (`ci-receipt-await-batch.ts` +
`fleet ci-receipt-await-batch` CLI + `fleet_ci_receipt_await_batch` MCP +
`ci-receipt-batch-replan`). Its only unique file is an unused duplicate module
whose contract is strictly weaker than the live one and which does not compile
against current master imports. Recommend the coordinator **close #3648 as
superseded — not merge**; this test file is the preservation evidence.
Disposition left to the PR coordinator per task scope.

- Node's `--permission` model is stable since v22.13.0, so Phantom's Node ≥22.15

  MIT→Apache-2.0 transition; current npm releases still carry MIT. Both states
